angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,127,034 km at 274.28 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 3.6459 +/- 0.0221 mas (same row, RUWE 1.27): 274.28 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.62 +/- 0.17 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-6 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 1,127,034 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.79 +/- 0.6 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-6 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6570 +/- 80 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-6 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-6 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-6.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.272, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
